title: Dangerous Goods Acceptance: Free Allowance and Chargeable Amendments
content:
## Clause

On a Dangerous Goods Acceptance file, the amendments that count for charging are the acceptance's declaration submissions of the amendment type whose outcome is signed. A declaration still waiting for the shipper's signature, one returned for correction and one withdrawn are left out of the count entirely.

The counted amendments are ranked by the moment they were signed. The earliest of them, up to the category's free allowance, cost nothing; each one signed after those is chargeable. Put as a number: the chargeable amendments are the signed amendments less the free allowance, and the figure never drops below zero.

## Free allowance per category

| Category | Signed amendments free of charge, per acceptance |
|---|---|
| AHL DG Limited Quantity | 1 |
| AHL DG Class 9 Standard | 1 |
| AHL DG Flammables and Corrosives | 1 |
| AHL DG Toxics and Oxidizers | 0 |
| AHL DG Compressed Gases | 0 |
| AHL DG Special Approval | 0 |

## Worked cases

| Category | Declaration file shows | Signed amendments counted | Chargeable amendments |
|---|---|---|---|
| AHL DG Class 9 Standard | two signed amendments | 2 | 1 |
| AHL DG Class 9 Standard | one signed amendment, one returned for correction | 1 | 0 |
| AHL DG Toxics and Oxidizers | one signed amendment | 1 | 1 |
| AHL DG Limited Quantity | no amendment at all | 0 | 0 |
| AHL DG Flammables and Corrosives | one awaiting signature | 0 | 0 |

## Points of judgement

**Which amendment is the free one when there are several?** The one signed earliest, within the allowance; later signatures are the chargeable ones.

**Does a withdrawn amendment use up the allowance?** No. Only signed amendments are counted.
